newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Interest rates push up NZ farm input prices - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Interest rates push up NZ farm input prices - SNZ.

text.p: The price level of all New Zealand farm inputs excluding livestock increased by 1.3 percent from the June 1996 quarter to the September 1996 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday in releasing the Farm Expenses Price Index.
This compared with an increase of 0.2 percent for the previous quarter.
The annual change from September 1995 quarter was an increase of 1.4 percent.

"The dominant contributor to the latest quarterly increase was a rise in interest rates. A much smaller contribution came from an increase in prices of materials used for repairs and maintenance, and higher farm rents," SNZ said.
"Partially offsetting price decreases were recorded for fertiliser and insurance premiums."

Over the September quarter, the level of input prices for dairy farms showed a 1.7 percent increase, sheep and beef farms a 1.4 percent increase, horticulture farms a 0.8 percent increase, and cropping and other farms a 0.7 percent increase.

Over the year to the September 1996 quarter, dairy farms and sheep and beef farms showed a 1.4 percent increase, horticulture farms a 1.0 percent increase, and cropping and other farms a 1.7 percent increase.
"The increase in interest rates over this annual period has had a major effect on the level of input prices for all farm types with the major increase occurring in the September quarter," SNZ said.
"A rise in local and central government rates and fees was also a major contributor to the increases for sheep and beef farms and dairy farms."

For all farm inputs including livestock, the latest quarterly movement was an increase of 1.4 percent and the annual movement was an increase of 1.3 percent. Livestock prices increased only 0.3 percent over the year.
